item.text:
# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan, 2024: 1B.4 evidence note

Overall read: favorable, but mostly indirect. I found several 2024 items showing Pakistan under Sharif actively engaging arms-control / nonproliferation / disarmament fora and publicly reaffirming multilateral restraint. I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Sharif repudiated, sabotaged, or cynically used these agreements.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Arms Control And Disarmament | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | Standing policy page; current version cites a May 2024 update | https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament | Pakistan’s official policy page says it supports CTBT objectives, a unilateral testing moratorium, FMCT negotiations, IAEA safeguards and reciprocal inspections proposals, UNSCR 1540 implementation, export controls, and non-discriminatory multilateral nonproliferation/disarmament norms. The page also says Pakistan published an updated nuclear-security booklet in May 2024 and joined the Nuclear Security Contact Group. This is the strongest evidence of support, though it is institutional rather than a single Sharif quote. | 1B.4; also 1B.3 |
| Favorable | Joint Statement on 6th Round of Pakistan-United Kingdom Dialogue on Arms Control & Non-Proliferation | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-05-16 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/6th-round-of-pakistan-uk-dialogue-on-arms-control-non-proliferation | Pakistan and the UK held a formal arms-control and nonproliferation dialogue, reviewed UN, CD, IAEA, and OPCW issues, and pledged continued coordination on multilateral fora. This supports a good-faith engagement reading. | 1B.4 |
| Favorable | Pakistan-China Bilateral Consultations on Arms Control and Nonproliferation | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-09-14 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/pakistan-china-bilateral-consultations-on-arms-control-and-nonproliferation | Pakistan held the 9th round of consultations on arms control and nonproliferation, covering global/regional security, cyber, AI, outer space, peaceful nuclear technology, and multilateral treaty forums. That is direct evidence of ongoing diplomatic engagement with arms-control mechanisms. | 1B.4 |
| Favorable | Prime Minister’s participation in the 79th Session of the United Nations General Assembly | Press Information Department, Pakistan | 2024-09-22 | https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/26508 | The government said Sharif would reaffirm Pakistan’s commitment to multilateralism and the UN role in global peace and security at UNGA. This is broader than arms control, but it supports a de-escalatory and institution-first posture. | 1B.4; also 1B.2 |
| Favorable | The visit of UN Disarmament Fellows to Pakistan | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-10-21 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/the-visit-of-un-disarmament-fellows-to-pakistan | Pakistan hosted UN disarmament fellows and briefed them on its stance on arms control, disarmament, nonproliferation, and its nuclear safety/security architecture. That is direct evidence of active engagement with the disarmament education and verification ecosystem. | 1B.4; also 1B.3 |
| Favorable | ‘Chill of a new Cold War’ is in the air, Pakistan leader tells UN Assembly | UN Geneva | 2024-09-27 | https://www.ungeneva.org/en/news-media/news/2024/09/98067/chill-new-cold-war-air-pakistan-leader-tells-un-assembly | Sharif’s UNGA remarks framed the global environment as a dangerous new Cold War and emphasized conflict, terrorism, and the need for diplomacy. This is not an arms-control agreement, but it is consistent with de-escalation politics rather than rejection of restraint. | 1B.4; also 1B.2 |

## Search gap

- I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Sharif opposed arms-control, inspection, nonproliferation, or disarmament agreements.
- I also did not find a 2024 event where he personally signed or announced a new treaty accession.
- The evidence is mostly institutional and diplomatic, so the safest conclusion is: supportive in posture and engagement, but with limited proof of new ruler-level treaty initiative.
